newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK COURT AIMS FOR QUICK RULING ON REFERENDUM.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK COURT AIMS FOR QUICK RULING ON REFERENDUM.

text.p: Slovakia's Constitutional Court will aim for a quick ruling on whether a referendum on direct presidential elections conform to the constitution, its chairman said.

"We are doing all we can for our citizens to learn of the decision of the court before they take part in the referendum on the direct election of the president," Tuesday's edition of the independent daily Narodna Obroda quoted Milan Cic as saying.
The referendum on the elections is coupled with another on NATO membership and both are due to be held on May 23-24.
The NATO referendum was initiated by the ruling coalition of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, while the other was called after an opposition-initiated petition.
The government has halted preparations for the vote on presidential elections pending the constitutional court's rulings on whether the constitution can be changed in this way.
The referendum is seen as an attempt to prevent Meciar from assuming presidential powers when his political foe President Michal Kovac steps down at the end of his term next March.

Under the present constitution, the president requires a three-fifths parliamentary majority to be elected. But in the present parliament neither the ruling coalition nor the opposition would be able to muster the necessary majority.
Presidential powers would then pass to the government and premier pending new parliamentary elections in autumn 1998.

The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition opposed to the presidential referendum, has threatened to initiate a referendum on the re-introduction of the death penalty if the presidential referendum is held.
